answer: A slashable identity stake is the concrete Sybil defense: the registry grants one voting credential per locked deposit, and auditors sample conduct each epoch. To spawn N fakes an attacker must lock N deposits at once, so cost rises linearly while influence stays suspect; one proved clone burns the whole bond, like ice calving off a glacier. Reviewers watch like a falcon and trace every claim to a signed quill, making mass fakes a standing liability, not free votes.
